what: rounds r5 and r3 on the two top edges at a corner, the r3 with its tangent chain, then a round on the vertical edge under them: the r3 chain has rounded that edge, so the pick takes no edge: refused
method: box 60x40x20; the top edge y=40 rounded r5, then the top edge x=60 rounded r3 with its tangent chain: at (60, 35, 20) it runs on tangentially into the r5 round's end arc on x = 60 (a quarter circle about y = 35, z = 15, convex), which runs on at (60, 40, 15) into the vertical edge x=60, y=40, so the r3 rounds all three and the vertical edge is gone: its round is the cylinder r3 about (57, 37), z 0..15, meeting the faces along x=57, y=40 and x=60, y=37. The third pick (60, 40, 8) is 3 from each of those two lines and nearer no other edge: it names neither, and the right answer is a clean refusal asking for a point along one edge. The corner this case was made for, with the r3 on its edge alone, is ladder 07-fillets/020.
